Subject: Invoice sender / portal onboarding question

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to the next step. Before we kick off onboarding, our AP team asked one operational question:

Who will be the canonical sender on the invoice PDF/email? They want to know if invoices will come from:
- billing@redwood.ai (Redwood centralized sender)
- the originating product team (e.g., infra@redwood.ai)
- or from a customer-specific sub-sender (billing+evergreen@redwood.ai)

AP also needs to decide whether to opt into your portal (preferred) or keep email copies. For larger vendors they prefer a staged approach: portal first for monthly invoices, with email fallback and a PO-exception path for one-off charges.

Can you confirm options and share any templates or a recommended enrollment plan? We also have a few PO exception scenarios (rush credits / one-off services) that need a defined handling flow.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Finance Ops Manager
Evergreen Retail

[Attachment: sample_po_2027-02.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@evergreen.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, AP Team <ap@evergreen.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 12:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sender / portal onboarding question

Hi Elaine — great to hear the team's ready to move forward. Short answer: we support all three patterns you listed, but we recommend one canonical sender per customer for consistency and AP reconciliation. Below is what we typically propose for a staged rollout plus a PO-exception path.

Proposal (high level):
1) Canonical sender: billing@redwood.ai as the default for Evergreen.
   - Benefits: predictable SPF/DKIM/Sender reputation, single point for automated attachments and metadata.
   - We can add a unique Reply-To (billing+evergreen@redwood.ai) if you want mailbox separation.

2) Staged portal enrollment:
   - Phase 1 (30 days): Portal opt-in for monthly invoices; email PDFs continue as CC for the first two months.
   - Phase 2 (60–90 days): Email copies disabled for AP inboxes that confirm acceptance; fallback enabled for exceptions.

3) PO exceptions workflow (one-off items):
   - For rush or non-standard charges, we recommend the PO Exceptions matrix (attached). Workflow summary:
     - AP flags PO exception -> Redwood CS intake -> Finance review -> Manual invoice routed to AP email with PO-exception marker in subject and a JSON metadata payload for your AR system.
     - Standard SLA: 48–72 business hours for manual issuance.

Attachments I’m sharing: invoice_sender_map_v1.xlsx (shows proposed sender mappings by entity) and po_exceptions_matrix.pdf (decision tree and metadata fields).

Next steps:
- Kimberly is our billing owner; Kim, can you confirm portal onboarding cadence and any technical prerequisites (SFTP, API webhook, or direct portal admin invite)?
- Elaine / AP: do you want the Reply-To alias or full separate sender? Also, do you want us to run a test invoice through the portal this week?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: invoice_sender_map_v1.xlsx, po_exceptions_matrix.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@evergreen.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, AP Team <ap@evergreen.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sender / portal onboarding question

Elaine — thanks Sean. A few operational notes from our side:

- Portal enrollment: we can invite up to 3 AP admins initially. Please send the names and corporate emails. Invitations come from no-reply@redwood.app; once accepted, you’ll see current month and prior 3 months of invoices in the portal.

- Technical options: API webhook push (preferred) or SFTP push. If Evergreen wants to consume JSON metadata, choose webhook; for legacy EDI/AP systems, SFTP bundle (XML/PDF) works.

- Sender choice: billing@redwood.ai + Reply-To alias gives the best balance. It keeps DKIM/SPF consistent and lets AP reply directly to your team. If Evergreen requires invoices to come from a corporate-branded address, we can do a delegated sender but that requires DNS verification (3–5 business days).

On the PO exception matrix: we flagged 3 cases that require manual action (rush credits, hardware one-offs, and legacy contract true-ups). If you want, Marco (cc’d on procurement) and I can script a short test case on Wednesday to exercise the manual issuance path.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
